title: region-pin-impact-storyboard-and-operator-templates
content:
Purpose
This is a working storyboard + operator template bundle to help product, sales-eng, legal, and SREs reason about concrete customer impact when a tenant is region-pinned and when enforcement modes change.

Audience
- Primary: SRE/operators responsible for pin enforcement and evidence packaging.
- Secondary: Sales Eng, Solutions, Legal (contracting), Product managers evaluating UX/rollout tradeoffs.

What this file contains (quick outline)
1) 3 short customer storyboards (low/medium/high churn risk) describing user-visible impact and operator signals to watch.
2) Operator templates for common enforcement actions (soft-pin alert, hard-pin failover, migration start/rollback).
3) Acceptance criteria checklist for launching a new enforcement mode or region.
4) Telemetry & evidence artifacts list (what to collect + sample queries).
5) Open questions and proposed experiments.

----
1) Customer storyboards (concrete vignettes)
A. SMB SaaS (low churn risk) — "Daycare CRM, US->EU pin"
- Context: Customer headquartered in EU but early data landed in US region during onboarding. They accept a pin to EU.
- User-visible: Slightly higher latency for admins in US during peak; archival flows show EU storage location.
- Operator signals to watch: pin-assertion logs (pin_request_id), slow-tail latencies from EU edge, KV-cache warmup time by tenant.
- Recommended operator actions: schedule KV-prefetch window, notify customer via template #smblow-latency, monitor for 24h then escalate if 95p latency > SLO.

B. Mid-market payments platform (medium churn risk) — "Regional failover during hard-enforcement"
- Context: Customer requires hard EU residency. During enforcement cutover a minority of sessions still route to hosted US nodes due to legacy tokens.
- User-visible: Payment confirmations occasionally fail (edge 500) and retries surface longer payment times.
- Operator signals: cross-region traffic tags, token-origin mismatch count, failed-auth events correlated with region mismatch.
- Operator template: apply transient client-side blocking for sessions with origin mismatch (soft block first), issue rollback-if-fail criteria after 30m, open a high-priority incident channel for Customer Success and Sales Eng.

C. Large enterprise (high churn risk) — "Pinned tenant with cache-eviction during migration"
- Context: Large tenant migrates archival store and requests pin enforcement window. Migration triggers large cold-cache behavior causing tokenized inference jobs to degrade.
- User-visible: Latency spikes and quota overruns triggering throttling; customer starts hitting support SLA.
- Operator signals: cache-eviction rate, model-autoscale events, queue-length growth, billing spike alerts.
- Recommended actions: enable migration surge capacity for pinned tenant (pre-approved burst), temporarily increase per-tenant rate limit, coordinate legal/sales for customer credit if SLA breached, and run postmortem with remediation items.

----
2) Operator templates (copy/paste-ready)
Template A: Soft-pin alert (automated)
- Trigger: tenant.pin_requested && enforcement_mode == SOFT && cross_region_request_ratio > 0.02 for 10m
- Automatic actions: email customer (template id: pin-soft-ack), create a ticket in PD queue (jira PD-xxxx), tag tenant telemetry with pin.transition.id
- Manual actions for operator: run "tenant-prefetch.sh <tenant>" to warm caches; monitor latency for 1h; if >SLO escalate to oncall.

Template B: Hard-pin enforcement step-down
- Prechecks: verify KMS key location, confirm backup snapshot present in target region, confirm network egress rules allow local connectors.
- Trigger: scheduled enforcement window OR automated enforcement policy
- Actions: 1) Mark tenant read-only in non-compliant regions; 2) Reject new sessions from non-target regions with HTTP 409 and structured error explaining pin; 3) Emit audit bundle (see telemetry section); 4) If rejection rate >0.5% and customer reports failures, run rollback procedure.

Template C: Migration rollback (fast fail)
- Trigger: any of the following within migration window: queue-length > 10k OR error-rate delta > 3x baseline OR billing-exceeded threshold
- Actions: 1) Re-enable previous region routing for in-flight sessions; 2) Rehydrate caches from snapshot; 3) Notify customer and run postmortem runbook.

----
3) Acceptance criteria checklist for new enforcement mode (launch gate)
- [ ] Telemetry instrumentation: pin_request_id, tenant_region_source, token_origin, request_region_header present in 100% requests in staging
- [ ] Operator runbooks validated in staging (2 oncall reps executed tests)
- [ ] KMS/Key residency verified and recovery workflow documented
- [ ] Data access logs exportable for legal (sample evidence package validated)
- [ ] Rolling rollback tested and completed within SLA window (test sim)
- [ ] Customer-facing messaging templates prepared for each channel (email, portal, support)

----
4) Telemetry & evidence artifacts (what to collect + example queries)
- Required signals (minimum): tenant_id, tenant_pin_state, request_region, token_origin, auth_status, latency_ms, error_code, cache_hit, model_variant
- Audit bundle contents: time window, signed routing decisions file, PK of key used (kms_location), sample request ids (redacted), operator action log
- Example Splunk/BigQuery queries (pseudocode):
  * recent-cross-region-requests: SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) WHERE request_region != tenant_pin_region AND timestamp > -1h GROUP BY tenant_id
  * token-origin-mismatch-rate: SELECT COUNT(*)/SUM(1) WHERE token_origin != request_region GROUP BY tenant_id
- Retention notes: keep audit bundle for 12 months by default for Enterprise customers; escalate to legal hold if subpoena flagged.

----
5) Open questions & proposed experiments
- Q: Should we proactively reissue short-lived tokens scoped to pinned-region to reduce mismatch windows?
  Proposed experiment: roll token-scope pilot for 10% of new signups and measure mismatch reduction and auth-failure regressions. Owner: Evelyn Park.
- Q: Burst capacity billing — can we auto-apply credits for SLA-detectable residency-induced performance regressions?
  Action: product + finance to prototype crediting flow; measure cost delta. Owner: Diego Morales.
- Q: UX: offering soft- vs hard-pin choice at onboarding vs contract stage — which reduces churn and support volume?
  Experiment: A/B test in trial signup. Owner: Liam O'Connor.

----
Appendix: Quick operator commands & links
- Commands (staging): tenant-prefetch.sh <tenant>, pack-audit-bundle <tenant> --start=... --end=..., dry-run-fallback <tenant>
- Important links: Confluence Residency Playbook (RESIDENCY-STRAT-0412), Pinning telemetry dashboard (dash/residency/pins), Migration runbook template (drive/migration/runbook-v2)

Notes / next steps
- Circulate to SRE oncall rotation for test-run next week.
- Product to align on acceptance gate revisions before next enforcement rollout.
- Legal to confirm audit bundle schema is sufficient for EU data discovery requests.

Unresolved (short list)
- Owner & billing flow for surge credits (Finance not decided).
- Exact sample size for token-scope pilot (requires engineering capacity estimation).

---
